original_question: Does there exist a Legendre function f: R^n -> [-infinity, +infinity] with full domain X = R^n such that f is not quadratic, yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev with respect to the Bregman distance induced by f? Equivalently, can there be a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre function whose gradient map grad f is nonaffine but still preserves convexity in the strong sense needed for every nonempty closed convex subset of X to have a unique right Bregman nearest point from each x in U?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 3: Does there exist a Legendre function with full domain such that f is not quadratic yet every nonempty closed convex subset of U is right D-Chebyshev? The problem is introduced already in Section 3, immediately after Fact 3.4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's target as an existence question about a full-domain Legendre function, excludes the quadratic case, and asks for the very strong property that every nonempty closed convex set have unique right Bregman nearest points. You also correctly noticed the link with the gradient map and convexity preservation, although the paper states that link as a consequence of a positive answer, not as an explicit equivalent reformulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
missing_details: The ambient setting is a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space X=R^J with its standard inner product, norm, and metric; the paper is not asking this in an arbitrary Banach-space setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
One should specify that f belongs to Γ_0(X) and is Legendre, and that U:=int(dom f); when f has full domain, dom f=X and therefore U=X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
The relevant discrepancy is the Bregman distance D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-<∇f(y),x-y>, with x in X and y in U. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

Right D-Chebyshev should be made explicit via the right nearest-point map: for each nonempty closed convex C⊂U and each y∈U, the minimization problem min_{x∈C} D_f(x,y) has a unique solution, i.e. the right nearest-point set is a singleton. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

The official formulation quantifies over every nonempty closed convex subset of U; your draft writes X, which is fine only after making the full-domain identification U=X explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

The paper does not present the nonaffine/convexity-preserving gradient-map statement as an equivalence. It is only noted as what would follow from an affirmative answer to Problem 3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

The nearest paper-faithful target is Section 8, Problem 3, motivated by Fact 3.4 and the surrounding discussion in Section 3; it should not be broadened into a general classification problem for all right D-Chebyshev sets. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
refined_question: Let X=R^J be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let f∈Γ_0(X) be a Legendre function with full domain dom f=X, set U:=int(dom f)=X, and define the Bregman distance by D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-<∇f(y),x-y> for x∈X and y∈U. For a nonempty closed convex set C⊂U, let the right Bregman nearest-point map be P^right_{f,C}(y):=argmin_{x∈C} D_f(x,y). Does there exist such a Legendre function f that is not quadratic and nevertheless has the property that, for every nonempty closed convex subset C of U and every y∈U, P^right_{f,C}(y) is a singleton; equivalently in the paper's terminology, every nonempty closed convex subset of U is right D-Chebyshev? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
justification: This refined question matches the paper's own open problem in Section 8, Problem 3, and it uses only the notation and hypotheses established in Section 1 and Section 3. The paragraph after Fact 3.4 is the immediate local context from which Problem 3 arises, and the paper's additional comment about the gradient map is only a consequence of a positive answer, not a proved equivalent restatement, so I did not keep your equivalently clause as an alternate formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
